sDescription: Handwritten lyrics by David Bowie brought in £89,000 at an Omega Auctions sale in Uxbridge, west London. The document included the late musician's edits, drafts, and notes for the songs 'Rock n Roll Suicide' and 'Suffragette City'. Both featured songs were part of Bowie's 1972 classic album Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars.

Ray Columbus, a singer-songwriter, television host, music manager, entertainer, and native of New Zealand, passed away at the age of 74. As the frontman for Ray Columbus & the Invaders, he performed on the 1964 track "She's A Mod", which achieved No. 1 status in Australia and marked the initial occasion a New Zealand group topped foreign charts. Throughout the 1960s, Columbus shared stages on tour with Rolling Stones, Roy Orbison, and The Newbeats.

Reports emerged stating that the sister of George Harrison resided in a pre-fabricated house and faced financial difficulties after her stipend from the The Beatles musician's estate ended roughly a year following his death. Louise Harrison, aged 82, acknowledged that she lacked access to her brother's wealth worth millions while residing with limited funds in rural Missouri. She confirmed she never contested the estate of her brother, stating, "I don't care about the money, it's been over ten years and I haven't made any ripples."

After a marriage lasting only four months, US actress Pamela Anderson sought a divorce from rapper Kid Rock. Through an announcement published on her website, the 39-year-old verified their separation.

Metallica performed the final concert of their 137-date 'Madly in Anger with the World Tour' at the HP Pavilion in San Jose, California. Generating $60,500,000 from ticket sales, the outing ranked as the fourth-highest grossing tour of 2004.

Tony McCarroll, the original drummer for Oasis, was unsuccessful in his attempt to sue the band's lawyers following his dismissal due to a delay in filing the claim. At the High Court in London, Judge Justice Gray informed McCarroll that the lawsuit could not move forward because the six-year statutory limit had passed.

Madonna performed at London's Brixton Academy, marking her first concert appearance in Britain in over seven years. Tickets were resold for upwards of £1,000, and internet auction site QXL.com auctioned off a single pair of tickets for £2,204.

David Bowie was named the musician's musician in an NME survey. Hundreds of leading pop and rock stars participated to vote for their greatest musical influence, placing Bowie ahead of The Beatles and alternative rock group Radiohead.
'Millennium Prayer' marked Cliff Richard's 14th UK No.1 single as he began a three-week tenure at the top of the UK singles chart, even though a majority of radio stations boycotted the track.

Jerry Edmonton, drummer for Steppenwolf, died at the age of 47 in an automobile accident near his residence in Santa Barbara, California. The band Steppenwolf released the single 'Born To Be Wild', which reached No. 2 in the US and No. 30 in the UK in 1969.
Taken from the 'Bodyguard' soundtrack, 'I Will Always Love You'—written by Dolly Parton—began a record-setting fourteen-week stint at No.1 on the US singles chart for Whitney Houston.

Nirvana recorded a performance for BBC TV music show Top Of The Pops in London. When asked to lip-sync 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' to a pre-recorded tape Kurt Cobain protested by singing an octave lower (he later confirmed he was imitating Morrissey from The Smiths), and attempted to eat his microphone at one point. He also changed some of the lyrics, exchanging the opening line "load up on guns, bring your friends," for "load up on drugs, kill your friends."

Bill Medley and Jennifer Warnes performed the duet "(I've Had) The Time Of My Life" for the movie "Dirty Dancing", and the track climbed to No. 1 on the US singles chart. The recording charted twice in the UK: reaching No. 6 in November 1987 following the movie's initial release, and subsequently hitting No. 8 in January 1991 after a mainstream television broadcast of the film.
David Bowie performed the second of four sold-out concerts of his Glass Spider Tour across Australia and New Zealand at Kooyong Stadium in Melbourne.
‘The One I Love’ gave R.E.M. their initial entry inside the Top 10 on the singles chart in the US.

The Tom Robinson Band performed their first live show at The Hope & Anchor in London. Their most successful hit, '2-4-6-8 Motorway', reached No. 5 in the UK in October 1977. Robinson currently works as a radio presenter as well.
The Sex Pistols made appearances on the UK television programs BBC TV's 'Nationwide' and ITV's 'London Weekend Show'.

John Lennon gave one of his final live performances by appearing alongside Elton John on stage at Madison Square Gardens in New York City. During the concert, Lennon played three songs: 'Whatever Gets You Thru The Night', 'I Saw Her Standing There', and 'Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds'.
Dave Edmunds topped the UK singles chart with his rendition of Smiley Lewis's 1955 hit "I Hear You Knocking." This recording was additionally the inaugural release for the new MAM record label.

New Morning, the 11th studio album by Bob Dylan, entered the UK charts and marked his sixth UK No.1. The record included the song 'If Not For You', which George Harrison recorded for his 1970 album All Things Must Pass, and which also served as the title track for Olivia Newton-John's debut album in 1971.

The Beatles recorded their final fan club recording together, titled 'Christmas Time Is Here Again!'. The Christmas records by The Beatles consisted of spoken and musical messages sent via flexi disc during the holiday season to official fan club members located in the United States and the United Kingdom.

The Shangri-Las achieved a No.1 position on the US singles chart with their 'teen death song', 'Leader Of The Pack'. Upon its release in the UK, the track was denied airplay by the BBC, likely because of its death theme, but nevertheless charted three distinct times: reaching No.11 in 1965, climbing to No.3 in 1972 after the BBC ban was lifted, and charting again at No.7 in 1976.

The Beatles played two evening performances: one initial concert at The Cavern Club located in Liverpool, followed by a second appearance at the 527 Club in Liverpool. The performance at the 527 Club took place on the top floor of the store as a dance event arranged for the employees of Lewis Department Store in Liverpool.

Elvis Presley began a six-week tenure at the top of the US singles chart with 'Are You Lonesome Tonight', which marked his third US No.1 single of 1960. A spoken section, loosely inspired by Shakespeare, was featured on the single.

Winifred Atwell achieved a No.1 position on the UK singles chart with 'Let's Have Another Party.' She made history as the first Black artist to top the UK chart and the first Black artist to achieve a million-selling record.

American singer-songwriter, record producer, actor, and rapper Trey Songz released his third album, Ready, in 2009. The album reached No. 3 on the Billboard 200, received a nomination for Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards, and featured 'Say Aah' (featuring Fabolous), which became a top ten single on the Billboard Hot 100.

American songwriter, composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist, Rostam Batmanglij from Vampire Weekend, who had the 2010 US & UK No.1 album, ‘Contra’ and the 2013 US No.1 album 'Modern Vampires of the City'. In 2016, Batmanglij announced that he had left Vampire Weekend to pursue solo projects.

Chamillionaire (born Hakeem Seriki), US rapper. He began his career in Houston's hip hop scene in the late 1990s and scored the 2006 US No.1 & UK No.2 single ‘Ridin’, which won Best Rap Performance at the 49th Annual Grammy Awards.

Matt Cheslin played bass for the English rock band Neds Atomic Dustbin, which scored a UK No. 16 single in 1991 with 'Happy'. The group's 1991 debut album, God Fodder, reached No. 4 on the UK albums chart. The band derived its name from an episode of the radio comedy programme The Goon Show.

Soundgarden drummer Matt Cameron joined Pearl Jam in 1998. When he was thirteen years old, he and friends formed a cover band named KISS, but they disbanded after receiving a letter from the management of the more famous band Kiss that threatened legal action.

Australian bassist Richard Grossman has performed on bass guitar for the Divinyls and Hoodoo Gurus, and was additionally a member of the Australian groups Matt Finish, Ghostwriters, Persian Rugs, The Kelly Gang, and Men At Work.

David Van Day is a singer who performed in the pop vocal duo Dollar, which secured the 1981 UK No.4 single 'Mirror Mirror'. Achieving ten top 40 singles on the UK Singles Chart, the duo experienced success during the late 1970s and 1980s. Previously, he was a member of the 1970s vocal group Guys 'n' Dolls.
David Jaymes is a member of the British pop band Modern Romance, which achieved the 1982 UK No. 4 single 'Best Years Of Our Lives' along with a series of other UK hits.

American singer Jeanette Hutchinson was a member of the group The Emotions, alongside her sisters Wanda Hutchinson and Sheila Hutchinson, who made up the original lineup. The band attained mainstream success throughout the 1970s. Their 1977 single 'Best Of My Love' reached No. 1 in the US and No. 4 in the UK, and won a Grammy Award for Best R&B Vocal Performance.

Hugh McKenna played keyboards for the Scottish rock band the Sensational Alex Harvey Band, which released the 1975 album Next and scored a UK No.7 single in 1975 with 'Delilah'. Throughout the 1970s, SAHB delivered a series of well-regarded tours and albums. In December 2019, McKenna passed away from cancer at age 70.

Canadian musician, actor, and comedian Paul Shaffer worked as David Letterman's musical director, bandleader, and sidekick across his Late Night television programs. Shaffer has recorded alongside numerous performers, such as Donald Fagen, Ronnie Wood, Diana Ross, B.B. King, Yoko Ono, Jeff Healey, and Cher. Together with Paul Jabara, he co-wrote the track "It's Raining Men" in 1982. The song later reached No. 2 on the UK charts for The Weather Girls in 1984.
Beeb Birtles is a member of the Australian band Little River Band, which achieved a US No.3 single in 1978 with 'Reminiscing', along with 12 other US Top 40 singles, and sold over 30 million records.

Randy Newman is an American singer, songwriter, arranger, pianist, composer, conductor, and orchestrator. As a recording artist, his hits comprise 'Short People' (1977), 'I Love L.A.' (1983), and 'You've Got a Friend in Me' (1995). He also composed songs such as 'Mama Told Me Not to Come' (1966), 'I Think It's Going to Rain Today' (1968), and 'You Can Leave Your Hat On' (1972). In addition, Newman composed film scores including the initial four Toy Story films (1995–2019), A Bug's Life (1998), the two Monsters, Inc. films (2001, 2013), and the first and third Cars films (2006, 2017). Paul McCartney once praised him as the greatest living songwriter.

American singer-songwriter Bruce Channel is best known for his 1962 No. 1 hit record 'Hey! Baby'. The harmonica segment in 'Hey! Baby', performed by Delbert McClinton, inspired John Lennon's playing on The Beatles's first single, 1962's 'Love Me Do', and also influenced later Beatles records.

Clem Curtis was a Trinidadian British singer and the original lead vocalist of the sixties soul group The Foundations. The band achieved the 1967 UK No. 1 single 'Baby Now That I've Found You' and the 1969 US No. 3 single 'Build Me Up A Buttercup'. Additionally, the group made history as the first multi-racial act to secure a No. 1 hit in the UK during the 1960s. Following a lung cancer diagnosis earlier in the year, Curtis passed away on 27 March 2017 at the age of 76.

Gary Troxel performed alongside the American vocal group The Fleetwoods, achieving a 1959 US No.1 and UK No.6 single with 'Come Softly To Me'. The Fleetwoods subsequently achieved a total of eleven hits on the US Hot 100.

Berry Gordy is the founder of Motown Records. In 1957, Jackie Wilson recorded 'Reet Petite', which was co-written by Gordy alongside his sister Gwen and writer-producer Billy Davis. Over the following two years, Wilson recorded an additional six songs co-written by Gordy, which included 'Lonely Teardrops'. Gordy put the earnings from his songwriting achievements back into production work. He found the Miracles, initially called the Matadors, in 1957 and started assembling a roster of successful talent. Throughout the following decade, he added acts to his label such as The Supremes, Marvin Gaye, The Temptations, The Four Tops, Gladys Knight & The Pips, Stevie Wonder, and the Jackson 5.
